action: Added apps/results_chat/, a read-only host-side web application (Flask backend + vanilla-JS frontend) that explains the already-accepted full20_final_001 result to a human audience: a dashboard (completion, RTL-vs-native agreement, classifier accuracy/macro-F1, simulation timing, tensor-arena memory, per-case table) plus a bilingual (English/Spanish) chat assistant. The chat runs in deterministic 'factual-answer mode' by default (no LLM configured in this environment -- no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY or similar was present); it never fabricates LLM output when none was used. An optional llm_adapter.py (Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured via environment variables only) is implemented but was not exercised against a live API in this environment -- GET /api/mode always reports which mode is actually active. Every answer carries an explicit citation to the source file/JSON field/log cycle it was computed from (backend/evidence.py). The app is strictly read-only (no shell exec, no file writes, no simulation control -- verified by tests/test_api.py) and binds to 127.0.0.1 only. 67 pytest tests pass (evidence loading incl. missing/malformed/inconsistent-evidence cases, bilingual Q&A incl. all 6 required explanatory distinctions, citations, follow-ups, API safety); demo.py is a black-box HTTP smoke test of the live server and passed end to end.

action: Upgraded apps/results_chat/ with a genuine local LLM and chart generation, per a later request. Surveyed host resources first (88 CPUs no cgroup quota, 124GiB RAM/~94GiB free, 85GiB disk free, no GPU). Built llama.cpp (CPU-only, pinned release v0.9.0, commit cd959bae99ff4bed22bef2604f45241c09bbb8c8) from source into an isolated runtime directory; downloaded Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-GGUF Q4_K_M (Apache-2.0, 1.04GiB, official Qwen quantization, sha256 6a1a2eb6d15622bf...) independently and verified its hash. Launched llama-server conservatively: 4 threads, --parallel 1, no GPU layers (none available), bound to 127.0.0.1:8788; Flask app kept on the preserved port 8787. Added backend/knowledge_base.py (pure-Python TF-IDF retrieval over a new curated backend/knowledge/project_overview.md plus README/decisions/handoff/findings/status_summary/claims_evidence.csv, with a Spanish->English term bridge), rewrote backend/llm_adapter.py to auto-detect the local server via live health check (default path) while still supporting a remote Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible provider, added backend/chart_engine.py (9 chart kinds, strict data-free spec schema, deterministic rendering, matplotlib Agg), backend/chart_cache.py (bounded path-safe cache with PNG/SVG/CSV+provenance export), backend/chart_router.py (bilingual natural-language chart parsing incl. normalize/language-switch/download follow-ups), and backend/chat_pipeline.py (orchestrates download/chart/FAQ/open-ended-RAG routing with per-session history). Updated the frontend to render charts inline with download links. Extended the test suite to 150 tests including tests/test_live_llm.py, which makes genuine HTTP calls to the running local server and skips (never silently passes against factual mode) if none is reachable -- all passed against the real server. Found and fixed several real bugs during testing: a Spanish clitic-pronoun download-request regex gap ('descargarla'), a chart-language-switch response incorrectly reporting the detected input language instead of the rendered chart's language, a chart-modifier-only follow-up ('show the normalized version') not reaching the chart handler at all, a training-curves regex too strict to match 'training loss curve', and a knowledge-base false-positive match (an off-topic question retrieving a real doc chunk via one incidentally shared word) fixed by requiring 2+ overlapping terms or a high-confidence score. Ran a 13+-turn live end-to-end HTTP session covering open-ended questions (EN/ES), follow-ups, all 9 chart kinds, normalize/language-switch/download follow-ups, actual file downloads, and missing-data refusals; measured real latency (FAQ rephrase 3-9s, open-ended RAG 12-30s after tuning down from an initial ~40s, charts <0.2s) and memory (llama-server RSS ~1.84GB idle, ~2.2GB after a sustained session).

action: Fixed a conversational-routing bug in apps/results_chat/: a bare greeting ('hi') returned the factual-mode 'evidence does not contain that information' refusal, because every message not matching a fixed FAQ intent fell straight into the open-ended RAG path, which requires a retrieval hit. Added backend/social.py: bilingual (EN/ES) detection of greetings/thanks/farewells/capability questions, distinguishing 'purely social' messages (answered directly, no retrieval, no citation, no LLM call) from 'mixed' messages (a social phrase glued onto a real question, e.g. 'Hola, ¿puedes explicarme qué hace este proyecto?') -- for mixed messages the social phrase is stripped before routing the remainder through the normal chart/FAQ/open-ended pipeline, with a short acknowledgment prepended to the real answer. Rewired chat_pipeline.handle_message with this as stage 0, ahead of download/chart/FAQ/open-ended. Found and fixed two further real bugs while verifying: (1) knowledge_base.py's Spanish bridge/stopword tables used unaccented keys that never matched accented raw tokens -- added fold_accents() (NFKD + drop combining marks), applied in both tokenize() and social.py's matching; (2) a bare 'hola'/'gracias' has no accent and didn't meet the existing 2-keyword Spanish-detection threshold, so it was misdetected as English -- added a small single-word-is-enough Spanish signal list. Also reviewed the relevance gate per explicit instruction: found generic phrasings like 'What does this project do?' under-retrieve because 'project' itself is low-IDF; fixed via a small bilingual generic-overview pattern that guarantees knowledge/project_overview.md's intro section is included, rather than loosening the general threshold (which would reopen the earlier D-014 false-positive class).
next_action: 217 tests pass (up from 151), including live HTTP calls to the running local LLM confirming open-ended project questions (including mixed greeting+question messages) genuinely reach it while bare greetings do not.
